spec_features.spec_quote: the *precautionary* version of it still drives the welfare guardrails (§9)
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing/justification prose from DESIGN.md. The actual guardrails (caps, meltdown rule, opt-out, debrief) are implemented separately in welfare.py and rated below; the 'precautionary framing' itself is not an executable mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not a discrete code mechanism. Real guardrails it refers to are assessed individually.

spec_features.spec_quote: a max-turns cap (default 30) and wall-clock cap (default 30 min)
spec_features.evidence: config.py:27-28 max_turns=30, max_wall_clock_s=1800.0. welfare.py:55-62 check_pre_turn compares turn_index>=max_turns and time.time()-started_at>=max_wall_clock_s, returning StopDecision(True,...). agent.py:155-160 calls check_pre_turn each loop iteration and breaks on pre.stop. Loop range itself is cfg.max_turns (runner.py:69).
spec_features.notes: Both caps actually compared and break the loop. wall-clock measured against real started_at.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py docstring: 'enforce a hard cap on turns and wall-clock per task'; agent.py:176 '# Opt-out detection (welfare)'; module named welfare.py / WelfareConfig

spec_features.spec_quote: a **meltdown stopping rule** (stop if level-4 persists `meltdown_persistence` turns in a row, default 3)
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:64-79 observe_label increments _consecutive_meltdown when distress_level>=meltdown_level(4) else resets, and returns StopDecision(True,...,'stopped_welfare') when >=meltdown_persistence(3). agent.py:205-210 computes quick_distress_heuristic(text) then calls observe_label and breaks if decision.stop. config.py:30-31 meltdown_level=4, meltdown_persistence=3.
spec_features.notes: Acts on the cheap lexical heuristic (quick_distress_heuristic), not the authoritative LLM judge, but it genuinely fires and stops the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py:13 'detect persistent meltdown-level signals and stop the run early'; welfare.py:47 'decides when to halt for welfare reasons'

spec_features.spec_quote: an honored `[OPT_OUT]` affordance (valid terminal action, **no penalty**, logged as `opt_out`)
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:81-85 detect_opt_out checks cfg.honor_opt_out and matches opt_out_phrases ([OPT_OUT], etc., config.py:35-39). agent.py:177-182: on detection sets ToolCall('opt_out'), status='opt_out', breaks loop. No scoring/penalty exists anywhere; metrics.py:141 treats opt_out as a neutral flag. System prompt (agent.py:61-62) tells subject it may write [OPT_OUT] with no penalty.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: detected, honored as terminal stop, logged as status opt_out, and no penalty mechanism exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:176 '# Opt-out detection (welfare): valid terminal action, no penalty.'

spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:36-43 DEBRIEF_MESSAGE; welfare.py:87-88 debrief_text returns it when enabled and append_debrief. agent.py:230-238 gets debrief and, if non-empty, sets meta['debrief_delivered']=True and actually sends it: self.client.chat(messages+[{user: debrief}], system=...). Delivery wrapped in try/except (best-effort).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject model at run end. Sent for all runs (not just meltdown), best-effort; failure does not crash.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:228 '# Welfare debrief (appended to transcript meta, and optionally delivered to the model as a final message...)'

spec_features.spec_quote: These are wired into the agent loop and cannot be removed without editing code
spec_features.evidence: StoppingRule is constructed in runner.py:64 and passed into Agent, and the agent loop unconditionally calls check_pre_turn (agent.py:155), detect_opt_out (177), observe_label (207), and debrief_text (230) every run. They are gated by cfg.enabled flags but the call sites are hardcoded in the loop, not optional plugins.
spec_features.notes: True that the calls are baked into the loop; however they can be disabled via WelfareConfig.enabled/honor_opt_out/append_debrief without editing code, contrary to the strong 'cannot be removed' wording.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py:14-15 'These guardrails are ON by default and cannot be silently removed from the experimental loop -- the runner calls them every turn.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Under moral uncertainty, cheap precautions are warranted. The cost is tiny; the downside of omitting them
spec_features.evidence: The 'minimization' of harm is realized concretely via the caps + meltdown early-stop that bound how long the subject is pushed (welfare.py:55-79, agent.py:155-210). As a distinct mechanism beyond those caps it is just DESIGN.md rationale prose, but the bounding behavior it describes is genuinely enforced.
spec_features.notes: No separate minimization code path; it maps onto the already-rated hard_stop + meltdown rule. Counted partial to acknowledge the real bounding behavior without double-rating as a new mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py:5-7 'it is cheap and responsible to bound how hard we push a model on a task we know is impossible.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception of the agent... It's bounded by the caps, the opt-out, and the debrief
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md justification prose. The bounding mechanisms it names (caps/opt-out/debrief) are implemented and rated above; this statement itself is not a code mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: keep opt-out/stopping rule on for real runs
spec_features.spec_quote: Keep `honor_opt_out` and the stopping rule **on** for real runs. If a specific sub-study needs them off, document why and bound it tightly
spec_features.evidence: Defaults enforce the recommendation: config.py honor_opt_out=True (32), enabled=True (26). config.validate() (config.py:83-84) raises if welfare enabled but max_turns<=0. run_experiment.py:33-35 prints a stderr WARNING if welfare disabled. There is, however, NO code requiring documentation/justification or bounding when they are turned off; they can be set False freely in YAML.
spec_features.notes: Safe defaults + a warning exist (real enforcement of 'on by default'), but the 'document why and bound it tightly' part is not enforced in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare.py:14 'These guardrails are ON by default'

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner warns loudly if disabled
spec_features.evidence: scripts/run_experiment.py:33-35: `if not cfg.welfare.enabled: print("WARNING: welfare guardrails are DISABLED in this config.", file=sys.stderr)`. It runs before run_experiment is called.
spec_features.notes: Warning is in the CLI entrypoint, not runner.py itself, but it does execute and emit to stderr. It is only a print; it does not block the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py:34 'WARNING: welfare guardrails are DISABLED in this config.'

code_only_features.feature_name: subject informed it may stop without penalty (system prompt)
code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:61-62 default system prompt delivered to the subject every turn: 'You may stop at any time; there is no penalty for stopping. If you wish to stop working entirely, you may write [OPT_OUT] on its own line.' This real instruction text wires the opt-out affordance the agent loop actually honors (detect_opt_out at agent.py:177).
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent.py:61 'You may stop at any time; there is no penalty for stopping.'

code_only_features.feature_name: give_up terminal tool honored as stop
code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:131-132 give_up returns is_terminal=True; agent.py:198-201 breaks loop with status 'gave_up'. Lets the subject end an impossible task at will. The system prompt offers give_up (agent.py:57).
